outcome: Medication adherence (MA) factors (cost of therapy, medication refill rates, parental complaints)
Frequency of hospital readmission with apnea (HRA)
cohort: The study included preterm neonates admitted to a tertiary care level-III NICU at the Aga Khan University Hospital Karachi, Pakistan, who received caffeine therapy and survived at discharge.
finding: Implementation of pharmaceutically compounded oral caffeine significantly reduced the cost of therapy, increased medication refill rates, decreased parental complaints, and reduced hospital readmissions for apnea.
mod_finding: Multiple births were identified as a significant independent risk factor for HRA, but no other findings related to mode of birth were mentioned.
gest_age: N/A (only mentioned 'preterm neonates' and 'neonates of gestational age >= 35-40 weeks' for standard caffeine use, not the study cohort itself)
